name: dang-59-file-local-imports
title: feat: file-local imports + LSP performance (first 8 commits)
head: 1058f48268e5984d5e97fc7f832b84a42c6219ae
notes: vito/dang#59 up to 1058f48, its 8th of 13 commits, before the fixes: +498/-181 over 13 files (make imports file-local, focused LSP inference, parse/mtime caches). Ground truth from history: the PR's later commits fixed the issues below, the bugs each with a regression test that fails at this head, so they are vetted real; the fixing commits are cited in each summary. PR #59 merged with all of them (head b0c575c).

issues.summary: Imports are file-local only during inference (as RunDir's new doc comment says): evaluation still flattens every file's forms into one masterBlock against a shared evalEnv, so imports from one file are installed for all of them and the runtime disagrees with the types. With a.dang `import Dagger` and b.dang `pub container: String! = "local"; pub useContainer: String! = container`, inference types b's container as String!, but at runtime SlotDecl.Eval finds the imported `container` already bound and keeps it, so useContainer is a Dagger Container. Fixed by a83340ce72 (fix(dang): scope imports file-locally at runtime: per-file evaluation through a CompositeEvalEnv, with TestRunDirImportedValueDoesNotShadowLocalDeclaration), then b0ffce338a (imports are not 'local' at eval time, for a file that imports and declares the same name).

InferDirectoryFilesFocused runs only the declaration phases for sibling files, but an unannotated computed variable (`pub answer = "ok".toUpper` in defs.dang) gets its type from the body-inference variables phase, not from variable signatures. So when main.dang (`pub use: String! = answer`) is the active LSP buffer, a valid directory that RunDir accepts shows a spurious `"answer" not found` diagnostic. Fixed by 131c9eaf7e (fix(lsp): infer sibling variable bodies), which runs the variables phase for siblings too and adds TestDiagnosticsResolvesUnannotatedSiblingVars.

declarationPhases = inferencePhases[:6] and bodyPhases = inferencePhases[6:] are hardcoded index slices into the phase list, so adding or reordering a phase silently misaligns both groups. Refactored in b0c575c49b (refactor(dang): name phase groups, not indices), which defines the groups as named slices and concatenates them.

sound.summary: runDirectoryPhases runs each phase across every file before starting the next, so every type name is registered before any signature resolves and cross-file references in signatures and bodies work regardless of file order.

Each file's composite env reads the shared dirEnv before the file's own imports and writes to dirEnv, so during inference a local declaration shadows an imported name and declarations stay visible to sibling files.
